test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Medha Patkar led a movement to protest against a large dam's construction? What was the name of the movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada Bachao Andolan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Medha Patkar** is a prominent Indian social activist who led the **Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA)**, a movement protesting the construction of large dams on the **Narmada River**, including the Sardar Sarovar Dam.
 
• The **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (Save the Narmada Movement) began in **1985** and primarily opposed the displacement of local communities and environmental damage caused by the dam's construction.
 
• The primary concern of the movement was the displacement of thousands of **tribal people, farmers, and villagers** whose homes and lands were submerged due to the dam projects.
 
• The NBA also highlighted the lack of proper **rehabilitation and resettlement** policies for the affected people and raised concerns about the ecological impact, including deforestation and loss of biodiversity.
 
• The movement gained international attention and raised significant debates on the costs and benefits of large-scale development projects, questioning their impact on marginalized communities.
 
• Despite its opposition, the **Sardar Sarovar Dam** was completed, but the NBA succeeded in bringing attention to the plight of displaced people and the importance of sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Medha Patkar:**

 
 
• Medha Patkar, born on **1 December 1954**, is a renowned social reformer and environmental activist.
 
• She founded the **Narmada Bachao Andolan** and has worked extensively for the rights of displaced people, particularly in tribal and rural areas.
 
• Her activism has also extended to other issues, including urban slum redevelopment and women’s rights.
 
• She has received several awards, including the **Right Livelihood Award** in 1991 for her efforts in environmental and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Sarovar Dam:**
 
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam** is a major dam on the **Narmada River** in Gujarat, India.
 
• It is part of the Narmada Valley Project, which includes the construction of several dams and canals aimed at providing **irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power**.
 
• The dam is one of the largest infrastructure projects in India and has been a subject of both praise and criticism due to its economic benefits and social/environmental costs.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Large dams like the Sardar Sarovar cause significant environmental impacts, including **deforestation, loss of wildlife habitats, and changes to river ecosystems**.
 
• Such projects also lead to the submersion of fertile agricultural lands and displacement of local communities.
 
 
 
• **Other Movements Led by Medha Patkar:**
 
 
• She has also been part of the **Right to Information (RTI) movement** and the **National Alliance of People's Movements (NAPM)**, which advocates for various social justice causes.
 
• Patkar has been vocal about issues related to urban displacement, particularly in Mumbai, where she campaigned against the demolition of slums.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chipko Movement:**

 
 
• The **Chipko Movement**, initiated in the 1970s in Uttarakhand (then part of Uttar Pradesh), was an environmental movement to **protect trees and forests** from being cut down.
 
• It involved villagers, particularly women, hugging trees to prevent their felling, hence the name "Chipko" (meaning "to hug").
 
 
 
• **Save Ganga Movement:**
 
 
• This movement focuses on cleaning and conserving the **Ganga River**, which is considered sacred in India but is heavily polluted.
 
• Initiatives under this movement include the **Namami Gange Programme**, launched by the Indian government to rejuvenate the river.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in **1973**, this project aims to conserve the tiger population in India and its natural habitats.
 
• It has led to the establishment of several **tiger reserves** across the country.
